editorial:
You meet Carl Mørck, a tired detective sent to Department Q, a basement office for old cases nobody wants. His new partner Hafez el-Assad is calm, smart, and surprisingly funny. Their first big case is Merete Lynggaard, a politician who vanished from a ferry five years ago. The movie feels cold, quiet, and tense, with a slow build that keeps pulling you in. You watch two very different cops learn to trust each other while digging into a mystery that everyone else gave up on.

The acting is strong, especially the way Carl and Assad balance gruff energy with dry humor. The pacing starts slow but gets tighter as clues appear, and the final stretch is gripping. Some scenes are dark and heavy, so it is not a light watch, but the mystery is smart and satisfying. If you enjoy Nordic crime stories, this is a great pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: Merete is alive, trapped in a pressure chamber by a man who blames her for his sister's death. Carl and Assad trace the clues to a remote location and arrive just in time. They free her after years of captivity, and the kidnapper is stopped. The final scenes show Merete reunited with her brother, while Carl and Assad earn respect and keep Department Q open for more cases.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Nordic crime thrillers and cold-case mysteries.
